scope: Recording timestamps, placement on the transport's bar lines, and compensation policy, measured for audio and MIDI against independent timelines

environment.machine: Kvant, pinned CI image (Qt 6.12, PipeWire 1.6.9), docker --network none
environment.device: owned private PipeWire server, software driver node only; no physical device

policy.timestamps: graph clock shared by the output, audio input and MIDI input in one driver group; the output publishes a transport anchor (graph frame, transport frame) each cycle; takes record the graph frame of their first cycle; MIDI events carry cycle frame plus offset
policy.placement: a recorded clip starts at the first bar line at or after the take's first frame: audio by the clip range (file keeps everything), MIDI by counting notes from it and leaving earlier notes out; Record from a stopped transport returns to the start
policy.compensation: none; physical converter and buffer latency are not measured here and not subtracted

verified_behaviors: Clicks emitted on transport bar lines land 0 frames from the recorded audio clip's bar lines, the same for every bar
MIDI notes emitted on beat lines land on their exact ticks in the recorded piano-roll clip
fl-live's own output, clicking on every bar line and fed back into its input, lands 0 frames from the recorded clip's bar lines without any anchor-based scheduling
Recording while running places the audio range and MIDI notes at the next bar line and reports notes left out before it; Record from a stopped transport starts on bar 1
limits: Software graph only: zero offset is the graph's scheduling, not a physical round trip; device latency (#19) is neither measured nor compensated. 4/4 only. The edit-bursts change only relaxes a timing-dependent assertion (saturation shown as refused controls or busy replacements).
